input.quote: In the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.1 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
input.rationale: Article 14.2 imposes fixed, formula-driven termination payments on PB (our party): 300% of Development Costs where SFJ terminates for PB's material breach (14.2.1), on PB's at-will termination (14.2.2), on bankruptcy termination (14.2.5.2) and on safety terminations attributable to PB (14.2.7); 150% on Change of Control (14.2.6) and compliance breach (14.2.8.1); 100% on Adverse Patent Impact (14.2.9); and Development Costs plus 25% annual interest on a JSC-decision termination (14.2.10). These are liquidated amounts payable by Customer and the breach-triggered multiples are punitive, so both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single capped early-termination fee) fail. Fixing the earlier draft's gaps, the revised Section 14.2.11 (i) deems every Development Cost-based amount a liquidated amount "however expressed as consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package", so the purchase-price framing cannot escape the cap; (ii) makes the cap computable as three (3) times average monthly Development Costs over the twelve months preceding termination, the only recurring cost run-rate in the Agreement; and (iii) expressly supersedes the retained 14.2.1-14.2.10 formulas and states the fee is the sole liquidated amount, removing the internal inconsistency. The override is scoped to Development Cost-based amounts so the Article 6 Approval Payments, Buy-Out Payments and all other commercial terms in those subsections are preserved verbatim. We leave 14.2.1's mutual right to pursue unliquidated damages at law intact: it is not a liquidated amount, sits outside this checklist, and also benefits PB as non-breaching party. Section 6.4 late-payment interest is ordinary default interest and is not flagged.

proposal.summary: Deem every Development Cost-based termination payment by PB to be superseded by a single early-termination fee capped at three times average monthly Development Costs.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 300%/150%/100% and cost-plus-25% termination payments are liquidated amounts payable by us, however they are labelled, so we have expressly superseded them with one early-termination fee capped at three (3) times average monthly Development Costs, stated as the sole liquidated amount payable by PB. Approval Payments and all other commercial terms are untouched; our preferred position remains no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties, and this three-month cap is our fallback.

ops.text: Liquidated Amounts. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, each amount payable by PB under Sections 14.2.1 through 14.2.10 that is calculated by reference to Development Costs (including interest thereon and any such amount expressed as consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package) is a liquidated amount, is superseded by this Section 14.2.11, and is payable solely as a single early-termination fee not exceeding three (3) times the average monthly Development Costs paid or incurred during the twelve (12) months preceding the effective date of termination, which fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by PB under this Agreement.

mappings.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
